title: Praise, O Praise Our God and King
description: Praise, O Praise Our God and King in Tonic Solfa to HEINLEIN, doh is F: the solfa with the words, staff notation, 8 verses and a piano.
about: Henry Williams Baker wrote these words. They were printed in the Evangelical Lutheran Hymn-Book (St. Louis, 1927), as hymn 297.
The book printed the words without tunes, marked Sevens (7.7.7.7), to be sung to any tune of that metre. This page sets them to HEINLEIN; any other Sevens tune fits them as well.
underlay: Praise, O praise our God and King, Hymns of a-dor-a-tion sing; For His mer-cies still en-dure, Ev-er faith-ful, ev-er sure.

lines: Praise, O praise our God and King,
Praise Him that He made the sun
Day by day his course to run;
And the silver moon by night,
Praise Him that He gave the rain
And hath bid the fruitful field
Praise Him for our harvest store,
He hath filled the garner floor;
And for richer food than this,
And the Spirit, Three in One!

licence: Public domain: Henry Williams Baker died in 1877.
credits: Words by Henry Williams Baker (1821–1877), public domain, as printed in the Evangelical Lutheran Hymn-Book (1927); set to HEINLEIN by NoteFusion, as words-only hymn books were sung.
